witness.note: Leges Henrici primi: Liebermann’s edited Latin text, from the manuscripts he names in Gesetze I, p. 547, note a, listed below
London, The National Archives (formerly the Public Record Office), E 164/2 (the Red Book of the Exchequer)
The original of the London collection, Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae (c. 1210), which survives in copies
London, British Library, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii (K1); but for the Quadripartitus and the London texts Liebermann’s K means Cotton MS Claudius D.ii (K2)
John Selden’s manuscript, now lost (known from Twysden’s variants)
Roger Twysden, in Wheloc’s edition of Lambarde’s Archaionomia (Cambridge, 1644)
London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 16.1
div.ab: Tam longe debet esse pax regis a porta sua, ubi residens erit, a quatuor partibus loci illius, hoc est: tria miliaria et III quarentene et IX acre latitudine et IX pedes et IX palme et IX grana ordei.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 559 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: am, davor roth N, obwohl Texthand T vorgeschrieben hatte, Sc; Nam übr.; Tam bessert Somner
am, preceded by N in red, although the text hand had written T as a guide letter, Sc; Nam the others; Somner emends to Tam
darüber Corr. IIII Sc; IIII Hg; quatuor übrige
IIII written above by the corrector Sc; IIII Hg; quatuor the others

div.ab: So far ought the king's peace to extend from his gate where he is residing, from the four sides of that place, that is: three miles and 3 furlongs and 9 acres in breadth and 9 feet and 9 palms and 9 barleycorns.
